newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASC charges former adviser, client.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASC charges former adviser, client.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Tuesday that former Sydney securities adviser Thomas Benjamin John Booth and his client Yussof Pepo Muraben had appeared in Sydney's St James Centre Magistrates court on charges relating to trading on the stock exchange.
The two men were charged with a number of offences of creating a false appearance of active trading in the securities of Charter Pacific Corp Ltd.
The ASC said the two men appeared in court on Monday and the matter was stood over until March 10 for a further mention.
The ASC said it alleged that the offences occurred in early 1994.
It said the charges were based on share market surveillance by the ASC and a subsequent investigation of suspicious trading patterns in Charter Pacific shares.
